key_insight: Self-powered microsystems will require energy harvesting to combine robust ambient-energy transducers with ultra-low-voltage power management and hybrid integration, not just better materials.
engineering_relevance: For IoT and wearable devices, the main challenge is system-level reliability: harvesting, rectification, impedance matching, storage, and cold-start operation must all work together under real-world conditions.
method: Surveyed triboelectric, piezoelectric/pyroelectric, indoor photovoltaic, and RF rectenna approaches.
Highlighted hybrid multi-source integration and metamaterial-enabled broadband RF harvesting.
Reviewed power-management and storage bottlenecks including PMIC cold-start and micro-supercapacitor/thin-film battery degradation.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites concrete performance gains such as liquid-solid TENGs that avoid wear, nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators that broaden bandwidth by over 300%, and multiband/broadband RF harvesting architectures.
watch_item: Many advances look promising at the materials level, but field durability, low-voltage start-up, and stable impedance matching remain major deployment risks.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
